sections.h2: How do Fort Myers owners usually sell?
sections.html:
Three roads lead out of a Fort Myers house: an agent's listing, a do-it-yourself sale, or a check from a buyer who accepts the place as you left it. Every road swaps something, whether that is price, calendar time, or the chance that a deal collapses.

Marketing the house draws the most eyes, and it also brings open-house traffic, inspection reports and a lender's appraisal. Cash skips those hurdles. The offer usually lands lower, so weigh how much a quick, quiet exit is worth to you.

  • Listing: wide exposure, many moving parts, timing tied to a lender.
  • Going alone: you take on the agent's work and the agent's risks.
  • Cash: few contingencies, no repairs, often a date you name.

sections.h2: What is the Fort Myers housing market like on paper?
sections.html:
Census data describes a city of 101,581 people in mid 2025, up 17.5 percent from the April 2020 estimates base of 86,424. That pace of growth shapes who is buying and who is renting.

The same Census page lists a typical owner-occupied value of $384,500 across 2020 to 2024 and a median gross rent of $1,580. About 49.1 percent of units are owner-occupied, so roughly half the city's households rent. Persons over 65 make up 23.2 percent of residents, workers average a 25.2 minute commute, and household income in the middle is $63,732 in 2024 dollars. Those figures point to a mix of long-time owners, retirees and working households, so buyers and renters for your house come from several groups.

sections.h2: How did the city of Fort Myers take shape?
sections.html:
The city began as an army post on the Caloosahatchee River and was incorporated on August 12, 1885. Before that, a fort camp was marked by a flag on February 20, 1850. Its older neighborhoods near the river carry that early street grid.

The Edison and Ford Winter Estates history of the city notes that Thomas Edison bought his riverfront property in 1885 and that Fort Myers broke from Monroe County in 1887 to create Lee County. McGregor Boulevard took its present name on July 15, 1914. Houses along those older corridors can be decades old, which affects what an inspector looks at: roofs, wiring, plumbing and windows.

The Fort Myers Community Redevelopment Agency says it has managed redevelopment trusts since 1984 to address blighted areas. Its listed programs include residential grants, commercial grants, historic preservation and affordable housing development. If your house sits in a redevelopment area, ask the agency whether a grant program applies before you sell or renovate.

sections.h2: Which Fort Myers offices handle permits and records?
sections.html:
The city runs an online permitting and licensing portal for building permits, and Lee County offices handle assessment, taxes and recorded documents. Start with the right office for the question.

  • Open or expired building permits: check the city's online permit portal, because a buyer's title and inspection process often asks about them.
  • Value, homestead and exemptions: the Lee County Property Appraiser, whose site offers a parcel search and explains homestead and portability.
  • Deeds and recorded liens: the Lee County Clerk's Official Records search, which the appraiser's site points to.
  • Tax bills: the Lee County tax collector, who can state what you owe.

Work done without a permit often surfaces during a buyer's inspection of older Fort Myers houses, especially roofs and electrical panels. A buyer's lender and insurer may ask for proof. Resolve it, or tell the buyer plainly, before the contract is signed.

sections.h2: What does Florida charge when a Fort Myers deed is recorded?
sections.html:
Florida taxes the deed itself at 70 cents for each $100 of consideration (s. 201.02(1)(a)). Every signer on the document is on the hook, so the contract should name who pays.

Recording at the clerk adds a page-based fee under s. 28.24(13), with extra trust fund and technology charges. The closing agent adds all of it up for you.

Property tax keeps its own calendar: value is fixed on January 1, a proposed-tax notice lands in August, and the bill follows in November. The Lee County tax collector can tell you the exact figure owed when you close.

sections.h2: What becomes of my homestead break if I sell?
sections.html:
Selling ends the exemption on that parcel, and the buyer's assessment moves to full market-based value the following January 1.

Under Save Our Homes, assessed value rises each year by no more than 3 percent or the inflation rate, whichever is smaller, and the 2026 figure in the state's chart is 2.7 percent. That protection stays with the old house, but you may transfer part of that benefit to a new Florida homestead if you establish it within three years of January 1 of the year you gave up the old one, filing DR-501T with DR-501 by March 1.

  • Homestead exemption: up to $50,000, filed on DR-501 by March 1.
  • Renting the home ends the exemption.
  • Portability is a benefit to plan before you close, not after.

sections.h2: What if the Fort Myers house is inherited or in foreclosure?
sections.html:
Both situations have fixed timelines in Florida law, and both can still end in a sale.

A small inherited estate may qualify for summary administration, a shortened court path under s. 735.201 that depends on the estate's size or the years since death. A probate attorney can say which route your family has. Creditor deadlines under s. 733.702 also run in the background.

After a foreclosure judgment, the clerk schedules a public auction within a set window (s. 45.031), and bidders must put money down at the sale. Selling before that date can end the case and protect what equity you have. Ask the Lee County Clerk about any surplus funds after a sale, since a homeowner may have a claim to money left after the lender is paid.

sections.h2: How do tenants affect selling a Fort Myers house?
sections.html:
Renters can stay through a sale unless the lease or notice rules end the tenancy first, and a rental share of about half the city's occupied housing means this comes up often.

Under s. 83.57, a tenancy by the month ends with at least 30 days' notice before the end of a monthly period. Year-to-year needs 60 days, and week-to-week needs 7. A fixed lease generally travels with the property.

Tell any cash buyer about the lease at the start. About 24.8 percent of residents are Hispanic or Latino and 21.8 percent are foreign-born per the Census, so a plain written agreement, with a translation where needed, keeps everyone clear on terms. Some buyers want the house vacant, and others will buy it with the tenant in place. Keep rent records and the signed lease ready.

faqs.q: Can a Fort Myers buyer take my house with the repairs undone?
faqs.a: Yes, cash buyers regularly do. The price will reflect their repair bill, so get the number on paper and set it beside a listing estimate.

faqs.q: Who pays the documentary stamp tax on a Fort Myers deed?
faqs.a: State guidance says every party to the document is liable, whichever side agrees to pay. In practice the contract assigns it, and the closing agent collects it at recording.

faqs.q: Does the Fort Myers owner-occupied rate affect my sale?
faqs.a: Only indirectly. With about 49.1 percent of units owner-occupied, many buyers are investors or landlords, and they tend to ask about rent rolls and lease terms.

faqs.q: What deadline should I know for homestead after a sale?
faqs.a: File DR-501 and any DR-501T with the Lee County Property Appraiser by March 1 for the tax year. Portability needs the new homestead to be set within three years of January 1 of the year you left the old one.

faqs.q: Where do I confirm my current tax balance?
faqs.a: The Lee County tax collector can state what is owed through your closing date. Bills go out in November.
